title: TierClass
description: The class of a storage tier a requester may ask for bytes, narrowest first: the requester's own store, another device of the same person, the household, a hub, a holon hub, a pool, a peer named by a doorway, a doorway. A class conflict between two records for the same tier keeps the narrower class (`TierRecord::merge`), and the default tier order compares class first (interfaces spec §A.2). A new kind of carrier is a new variant here, which is a spec change. Source of truth: this schema; Rust mirror `eprfs_core::TierClass` (eprfs-core/src/tier.rs, kebab-case serde, Ord in this order). Not named in §2.G's enum list; added because objects/tier-record's `class` needs a referenced vocabulary (CONVENTIONS rule 7). Carries neither `_dna` nor `_codegen`: it is a field vocabulary for the placement wire schemas, generated only as a TypeScript union where those schemas inline it, and adds no constant to schema-enums.ts. Not yet pinned: no test holds the Rust enum equal to this list (follow-on: a case in a test crate that depends on eprfs-core, such as eprfs-serve's tests).
